Vs.

full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J: This Rule is directed against the order dated 22.4.1989 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Uzirpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1987 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereby the learned Assistant Judge allowed the opposite party's application for amendment of the application. 

 2. The opposite party as pre-emptor filed a case for pre-emption in the Second Court of Munsif, Barisal being Pre-emption Case No. 191 of 1984, against the present petitioners and others. The said case was eventually transferred to the Court of the Assistant Judge, Uzirpur and was re-numbered as Pre-emption Case No. 26 of 1985. The said pre-emption case was eventually allowed ex-parte on 20.4.1987. The present petitioners thereafter filed Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1987 setting aside the ex-parte order allowing pre-emption. 

 3. The petitioner contested the case by filing written objection stating inter alia that summons duly served upon the pre-emptee and she had full and complete knowledge about the proceedings and he was never prevented by any sufficient cause when the case was called on for ex-parte disposal. 

 6. Mr. Md. Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that since on two other earlier occasions the pre-emptee-petitioner's applications for amendment were rejected by the trial Court on that there is absolutely no new ground for entertaining and allowing the third application of the pre-emptee, such prayers being earlier rejected by the Court, the learned Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order arbitrarily and illegally and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that having regard to the fact that the pre-emptee-petitioner has already examined three witnesses, including herself, the new statements which are now sought to be incorporated by way of amendment were never referred to by any of the witnesses, allowing of the pre-emptee-opposite party to make out a new and inconsistent case at this belated stage will totally change the character of the pleadings and the nature of the case and as such the learned Assistant Judge seriously erred in law in allowing the said prayer in an arbitrary manner and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 8. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before me the petition for amendment under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure as well as the original application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure which has been marked as Annexure-B to the petition. In the original petition for setting aside the ex-parte decree under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure it has been specifically stated that after coming to learn about the pre-emption case she engaged an Advocate to defend her in the case and took necessary steps in the matter. It has also been specifically admitted therein that the Advocate's clerk duly informed her of the dates of the case but on the fateful date of peremptory hearing of the case she could not appear before the Court due to her illness. Now she is taking a new and totally inconsistent defence by stating that she did not receive any summons in the case and she was totally ignorance about the proceedings of the pre-emption case. Law does not permit an applicant to take a completely inconsistent and contradictory defence under the garb of a relief under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Amendment of pleadings is regulated by Order 6, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Court enjoys wide discretion in allowing amendments at any stage of the proceeding provided that it does not change the nature and character of the suit or the pleadings or it does not cause unnecessary prejudice to the opposite party. Amendment is also allowed when in court finds that the proposed amendment is necessary for complete and effective adjudication of the suit. The proposed amendment is not only inconsistent and contradictory but it also takes way the very basis of the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It also appears from the record that on two other previous occasions the pre-emptee's applications for amendment were disallowed by the Court on assigning cogent reasons. In the impugned order the learned Assistant Judge has not assigned any reason whatsoever to justify the proposed amendment. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge passed the impugned order in a most careless and casual manner without applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the law bearing on the subject. 

 10. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the impugned order dated 22.4.89 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Uzirpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1987 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is set aside. 

 11. The learned Assistant Judge is directed to dispose of the miscellaneous case with utmost expediency, preferably within three months from the date of receipt of this order, without allowing adjournments to the parties except on compelling reasons.
